title: The topos universal property of a supplied qcqs etale presentation
statement: Let I be a small nonempty cofiltered category and D : I → Scheme a diagram whose schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and [def-weil-size-convention]. For any supplied Presentation P of D [def-per-qcqs-etale-limit-presentation], its projection cone satisfies IsToposLimit: every pseudocone from a Grothendieck topos in the stated containing universes factors through P, and every compatible family of direct-image natural transformations lifts uniquely to a natural transformation of the factors. This is exactly the two conjuncts of IsToposLimit in [def-per-qcqs-etale-limit-presentation]. The presentation is an input, not an asserted output, and no enough-points or reindexing conclusion is included.

source.place: Tags 09YL and 0A35; ILO XX 4.4, printed p.373 (literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf, PDF p.379).

proof.text: The stage categories have finite limits, computed under their evaluation in qcqs etale objects, and scheme pullback preserves them. The structure functors to the category colimit preserve finite limits: lift a finite diagram to one stage; the Hom calculation for filtered category colimits identifies maps into its proposed limit with the finite limit of the Hom sets, since filtered colimits of sets commute with finite limits. For the arbitrary object-and-arrow colimit supplied by P, transfer this calculation from the canonical one through the equivalence given by pseudococone restriction. Stage covers and their images are exactly those specified by P.stageCover_iff and P.cover_iff.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal E$ be any Grothendieck topos and $q_i:\mathcal E\to(Y_i)_{\mathrm{et}}$ a pseudocone with invertible comparisons satisfying the cocycle. Put $A_i(U)=q_i^{-1}(h_U^\#)$. By [lem-per-lex-cover-functor-extension] these functors preserve finite limits and covers; restriction of the inverse-image comparisons gives their coherent comparisons. The same lemma identifies the site functor of $p_i^{-1}$ with $U\mapsto h_{u_iU}^\#$: its extension has right adjoint $F\mapsto(U\mapsto F(u_iU))$, the projection direct image of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites].

source.place: Tags 00X6, 03A1, 00WS, 0A35; inverse images and their restrictions to associated representables.

proof.text: By [lem-per-filtered-category-pseudococones] the coherent $A_i$ give a functor $A:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$, unique up to the specified isomorphisms. Its restrictions are isomorphic to $A_i$. Every finite diagram and finite cover comes from a stage (Steps 1 and 3), so $A$ preserves finite limits and sends covers to jointly epimorphic families. Apply [lem-per-lex-cover-functor-extension] to obtain $q:\mathcal E\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$. Its restrictions identify $p_iq$ with $q_i$ and their cocycle. The two equivalences also extend each compatible family of natural transformations uniquely and preserve their identities and composites. Adjunction mates reverse the inverse-image transformations to the direct-image convention in [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Thus composition with the $p_i$ is an equivalence between geometric morphisms into $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ and pseudocones to the stage topoi, naturally in $\mathcal E$. This is the 2-categorical inverse-limit universal property.

Identity reindexing compares arbitrary strictifications. Scheme isomorphisms preserve qcqs. No affine-transition or limit-scheme hypothesis is introduced.
